[REVIVED] Dormant-pool match (20260624-2, Signals: quality bought with wall-clock time, accuracy-only leaderboards, latency end-to-end wall-clock reporting axis, per-task time-to-completion disclosure). Colibri publishes its throughput cost in the same breath as its capability claim: 0.05 to 0.1 tokens per second on a 12-core machine, community reports reaching 1.23 on high-end hardware, and the author's own framing that this is batch-job territory rather than interactive chat.
Stating wall-clock alongside what a system can run -- rather than reporting the capability alone and leaving the time cost implicit -- is the disclosure norm this call expects benchmarks to formalize, and here it arrives voluntarily from the project itself. It is a project README rather than a leaderboard column, and no orchestration benchmark added a latency field today.

reference_links.label: GitHub - JustVugg/colibri

bridge.narrative: The disclosure norm arrives voluntarily and from an unexpected direction. Colibri states its throughput cost in the same breath as its capability claim -- 0.05 to 0.1 tokens per second, community reports to 1.23 -- and the author frames the result as batch-job territory rather than letting the time cost stay implicit.
bridge.remaining_gap: This is a project README, not a benchmark column; no evaluator formalized a latency or cost-per-task axis for orchestration parity claims today.

prediction_ref.short_label: Local-LLM runtimes ship in-model speculative decoding on by default by Q2 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary:
[REVIVED] Dormant-pool match (20260705-1, Signals: llama.cpp vLLM MLX-LM opt-in, LM Studio, Ollama, paired-draft on-by-default, on-device-to-hosted throughput gap). Colibri ships speculative decoding in its stated feature set alongside MLA and DSA sparse attention, grammar-forced generation and optional CUDA and Metal backends -- a brand-new local engine treating speculative decoding as table stakes rather than as an advanced opt-in knob.
It also sharpens the throughput gap this prediction turns on, since 0.05 to 0.1 tokens per second marks the extreme end of what local users will trade away for capacity. The gap to the call: Colibri is a young dependency-free C project rather than one of the mainstream runtimes named, and its speculative decoding is a listed capability, not a documented on-by-default path.

reference_links.label: GitHub - JustVugg/colibri

bridge.narrative: A brand-new engine lists speculative decoding in its baseline feature set alongside sparse attention and grammar-forced generation -- treated as table stakes rather than an advanced knob, which is how a technique becomes a default. But at a tenth of a token per second the speedup barely registers, and Colibri is not one of the named mainstream runtimes.
bridge.remaining_gap: No second mainstream runtime flipped speculative decoding to on-by-default in release notes; Colibri lists a capability, not a documented default.

prediction_ref.short_label: Snowflake ships a metered Claude-in-Cortex governed-data agent tier by Q4 2026

validation_rows.evidence_summary:
[REVIVED] Dormant-pool match (20260602-2, Signals: governed data no egress, compliance wedge finance healthcare public-sector, credit-based consumption SKU, per-agent-run per-token pricing, named growth line). Both halves of the pattern appear today under different names. Anaconda's acquisition of Kilo Code builds the governed-agent tier -- agent orchestration paired with package provenance and a policy layer so enterprises can audit what their coding agents do and which models they call -- while Anthropic puts Pro and Team Standard subscribers on a one-time $100 credit and then API rates, credit-metered agent access shipping as a mainstream billing shape.
The governance wedge and the metered consumption SKU are both being validated in the same week, just not by Snowflake. Nothing today names Cortex, a Claude-in-Cortex integration, or a Snowflake agent tier of any kind.
